question: What is the primary characteristic that makes skeletal muscle different from smooth muscle?

options.A: It is found exclusively inside blood vessel walls
options.B: It lacks any visible striations under a microscope
options.C: It can contract entirely without any nerve supply
options.D: It is under voluntary conscious control

explanation: Skeletal muscle is consciously controlled by the somatic nervous system, unlike smooth muscle which works automatically. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h1)

question: Besides body movement, what is another vital function of skeletal muscle?

options.A: Regulating blood pH through bicarbonate storage
options.B: Filtering metabolic waste products from the blood
options.C: Producing red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.D: Generating body heat to maintain core temperature

explanation: Muscle contraction requires energy, and much of that energy is released as heat, which helps keep the body warm. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which connective tissue layer wraps around an entire skeletal muscle?
explanation: Think of the epimysium as the tough outer coat that wraps up the whole muscle, keeping it safe and secure!

question: What structure is formed when the epimysium, perimysium, and endomysium extend beyond the muscle belly?

options.A: A ligament that connects bone to bone
options.B: A joint capsule that lubricates movement
options.C: A tendon that attaches muscle to bone
options.D: A bursa sac that reduces friction

explanation: The connective tissue wrappings merge at the ends of the muscle to form strong tendons that anchor muscles to bones. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the specialized name for the plasma membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber?
explanation: The sarcolemma is the cell membrane surrounding a skeletal muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum inside a muscle fiber?

options.A: Anchoring the muscle to nearby bone tissue
options.B: Transmitting nerve impulses along the surface

explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum holds calcium ions until an electrical impulse triggers their release to start contraction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: What protein makes up the thick filaments in a sarcomere?
explanation: Thick filaments are composed of the protein myosin, which features small heads that pull on thin actin filaments. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h4)

question: What happens to the length of thin and thick filaments during muscle contraction?

options.A: They stretch out to make the muscle longer
options.B: They shorten significantly as the muscle contracts
options.C: They dissolve completely and reform afterward
options.D: They slide past each other and stay the same length

explanation: The sliding filament theory states that filaments do not change length; they simply overlap more as they slide past each other. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h4)

question: What chemical neurotransmitter is responsible for signaling a skeletal muscle fiber to contract?
explanation: Acetylcholine is released at the neuromuscular junction to transmit the nerve signal to the muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the direct result of acetylcholine binding to receptors on the motor end plate?

options.A: Calcium ions are pumped out of the cell
options.B: Sodium ions rush into the muscle fiber
options.C: The nerve ending absorbs the muscle cell
options.D: Myosin heads detach from the actin filaments

explanation: ACh opens chemically gated channels, letting sodium flood inward to start the electrical action potential in the muscle cell. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h5)

question: What molecule is the immediate source of chemical energy used for muscle contraction?
explanation: ATP supplies the necessary energy for myosin heads to move and detach during the contraction cycle. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why does high-intensity exercise without enough oxygen lead to muscle fatigue?

options.A: The motor neurons stop producing acetylcholine forever
options.B: Lactic acid builds up and energy supplies run low
options.C: The bones dissolve inside the connective tissue wrappings
options.D: Muscle fibers permanently lose all of their calcium

explanation: Anaerobic metabolism produces lactic acid and uses up energy stores quickly, contributing to cellular fatigue and soreness. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which skeletal muscle fiber type is best suited for long-distance endurance running?
explanation: Slow oxidative fibers rely on aerobic respiration, resist fatigue well, and power endurance activities like marathons. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h7)

question: A weightlifter performing heavy one-rep maximum lifts relies primarily on which muscle fiber type?
explanation: Fast glycolytic fibers generate quick, powerful contractions using anaerobic pathways, perfect for heavy lifting and short sprints. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h7)
